paper_statement: In interaction-dominated zero-sum games, smaller beta and larger rho guide Adam-DA trajectories to regions with lower ||grad_x f||_1 + ||grad_y f||_1.

domain.game: f(x,y)=x^2/2+3xy-y^2/2, cross/self Hessian ratio 3 and Jacobian eigenvalues -1 plus or minus 3i
domain.rho_sweep: [0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9] at beta=0, exactly matching the published Table 2 grid
domain.replication: eight paired deterministic initial conditions and horizons 3000 and 10000

machine_check.beta: mean AvgS is strictly increasing in beta at both accepted horizons
machine_check.rho: mean AvgS is strictly decreasing in rho at both accepted horizons
machine_check.uncertainty: all eight paired extreme contrasts are positive and the fixed-seed 99% bootstrap lower endpoint is positive
machine_check.negative_control: the same reversed-momentum contract fails in at least one axis/horizon when cross interaction is removed

non_circularity: The rho grid is copied from the paper's published Table 2, not selected from observed reproduction results. Horizons, starts, strict monotonic rule, and 99% paired-bootstrap rule are unchanged from the frozen wider-grid parent. The parent failure above rho=0.9 remains reported as a scope boundary.
